entry: Actuator liveness group, alias and overall HTTP health

questions.history: Set the unrelated sentinel to DOWN with all other indicators UP and probe membership implicit.
questions.prediction: The report predicts that the old customized liveness group admits the unrelated failure. Both merged liveness routes should return HTTP 200 with `status=UP`, while the overall health endpoint reports DOWN.
questions.basis: The requested path changes routing. Default liveness depends on `livenessState`; the overall endpoint confirms that the failing indicator was active.
questions.refutation: Either merged probe route reports DOWN or 503, or `/alive` fails to resolve while the canonical probe works.

questions.history: Add explicit `management.endpoint.health.group.liveness.include=livenessState,sentinel` and leave sentinel DOWN.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should report DOWN at the probe and use HTTP 503 with the default status mapping.
questions.basis: An explicit member with DOWN participates in the aggregate.
questions.refutation: Either revision masks the explicitly included failure or the two liveness routes disagree.

questions.history: Return to implicit membership. Toggle only the sentinel from DOWN to UP and repeat all three requests after each change.
questions.prediction: On the merge the overall status should change from DOWN to UP, while both liveness routes stay UP.
questions.basis: The independent public summary proves the sentinel actually changed, while the liveness inputs stayed fixed.
questions.refutation: A sentinel transition changes either liveness response, or the alias disagrees with its canonical endpoint.
